title: SLA-adaptive-priming-and-graceful-recovery-playbook
author: Priya Raman
body:
Overview:

This playbook documents an operator- and automation-first approach for detecting impending SLA violations, priming the inference runtime to reduce tail-latency impact, and performing a controlled, graceful recovery. It is intended for platform operators, SREs, and on-call engineers who maintain the Redwood serving runtime and platform traffic router.

Goals:
- Prevent SLO burn from short-lived token surges or cache misses by proactively priming caches and model variants.
- Provide a deterministic, auditable sequence of automated and manual actions to restore SLOs within 10 minutes for transient degradations.
- Avoid wholesale model swaps unless absolutely necessary; prefer traffic steering, batching tuning, and targeted priming first.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to multi-tenant inference pools (hosted + dedicated) with KV-prefix caching enabled and multi-model fallback routes configured.
- Not intended for long-running hardware failures (GPU OOMs, node crash) — see hardware-evacuation runbook.

Definitions and key signals:
- SLO (service-level objective): 99th percentile request latency <= 350ms for interactive text-generation routes; token-generation P95 per-token latency <= 75ms for streaming routes.
- SLI burn: an error budget depletion rate of >1% per 5m window or 10% increase in p99 latency vs baseline for >3 consecutive 1m windows.
- Priming: targeted warmup actions (KV cache prefetch, micro-batching synthetic prefix requests, JIT kernel warm-up) that reduce cold-path latency for a given model/tenant.
- Fallthrough model variant: a smaller or quantized variant that preserves correctness under degraded throughput.

Owner and contacts:
- Primary owner: Eng-Platform (operator runbooks) — Priya Raman (oncall/lead)
- Secondary: Serving Runtime (latency triage) — Evan Kline
- Pager: #platform-oncall in Slack, PagerDuty rotation group: platform-sre-team

Required dashboards and alerts (precondition):
- p99 request latency per-route (1m/5m windows)
- SLI burn rate dashboard by tenant
- KV cache hit rate by tenant and prefix
- Model variant fallback count and dispatcher queue depth

Alert thresholds (example):
| Alert name | Trigger | Initial severity | Escalation window |
|------------|---------|------------------|------------------|
| p99-latency-spike | p99 > 420ms for 3 consecutive 1m aggregation | Sev2 | 5m |
| slo-burn-fast | error budget burn rate > 2% in 5m | Sev1 | 2m |
| kv-cache-threshold | prefix hit-rate < 50% for 2m | Sev2 | 10m |

Note: threshold values are tenant- and route-specific. See tenant SLA mapping in the SLO registry.

Automated preflight checks (run by orchestration before priming):
1) Verify cluster capacity glance: node utilization < 92% and GPU memory headroom >= 10% across target pool.
2) Confirm model-variant compatibility: primary variant and fallthrough variants available in registry and marked compatible for route.
3) Confirm telemetry ingestion alive for p99, kv-cache metrics (no more than 30s lag).

Priming play sequence (automated + operator steps):
1. Detection and context capture (automated)
   - When p99-latency-spike or slo-burn-fast fires, orchestration creates an incident context bundle containing: top-5 affected routes, tenant IDs, recent model-variants used, kv-prefix hit-rate snapshot, and recent batch sizes. This bundle is attached to the incident page.

2. Fast mitigation (automated) — T+0..T+90s
   - Action A1: Trigger KV-prefetch for hot prefixes (based on top-10 prefixes by recent QPS). Implementation: orchestration issues a prefetch job that issues synthetic prefix requests at low QPS (0.5-2 req/s) with modeled token-length distribution.
   - Action A2: Temporarily reduce max-batch-size for affected routes by 25% to reduce variance in latency (config via per-route config API).
   - Action A3: Increase dispatcher soft-priority for latency-sensitive tenants by toggling a per-tenant hint flag (TTL 5m).
   - Roll-forward observability: create a synthetic SLI probe that runs once per 15s and reports p95/p99.

3. Secondary mitigation (operator-assisted) — T+90s..T+5m
   - Operator review checklist (runbook steps):
     a) Pull incident context bundle.
     b) Confirm that KV-prefetch jobs started and show improving hit-rate.
     c) If hit-rate not improving, run targeted prefix prefetch for the top failing prefix with larger synthetic requests (mimic realistic prefix lengths).
     d) Validate that CPU/GPU load did not spike above safe thresholds; if load spikes, abort prefetch and proceed to next action.

4. Traffic steering to fallthrough variants (operator + automated) — T+3m..T+10m
   - Criteria to cut traffic: persistent p99 > 420ms after priming and batch tuning for 3 consecutive 1m windows, or SLI burn rate remains > 2% for 10m.
   - Action B1: Canary route 10% of traffic to fallthrough (quantized) variant for 5m and monitor quality regressions via prompt-level quality probes.
   - Action B2: If quality probe signal stays within acceptable delta (see quality thresholds below), ramp to 50% over next 10m.
   - Action B3: If quality regressions exceed threshold, rollback fallthrough routing and instead initiate capacity-based mitigation (burst capacity request to Dedicated pool).

Quality monitoring and thresholds for fallthrough models:
- Use rouge/embedding-sim similarity suite on a holdout of 200 recent prompts representative for the tenant.
- Acceptable delta: mean embedding cosine similarity >= 0.92 and top-1 token disagreement <= 3%. If either fails, mark as blocked.

Rollback and graceful recovery steps:
- If fallthrough routing results in unacceptable quality or p99 does not improve, perform one of the following in order of preference:
  1) Invoke emergency scale-up (burst to dedicated capacity with SLA contract) — operator requests via capacity API.
  2) Perform targeted request-level admission control: degrade non-latency-critical features (background embed jobs, scheduled batch jobs) for affected tenant pool.
  3) As last resort, issue controlled tenant throttling with clear communication via customer-integrations (notify via webhook and dashboard banner).

Operator CLI commands and examples:
- Prefetch job kick: rwctl prefetch start --pool inference-pool-eu-1 --prefix "cust/123/conv" --qps 1 --duration 600
- Reduce batch size: rwctl route update --route-id routes/text-gen-interactive --max-batch 48
- Ramp fallthrough: rwctl route split --route-id routes/text-gen-interactive --variant small-quant-1 --weight 10 --duration 300
- Emergency scale: rwctl capacity request --pool inference-pool-eu-1 --gpus 8 --type burst --reason "SLO-burn mitigation"

Operator decision matrix (quick reference):
| Symptom | Triage check | First action | If fails |
|---------|--------------|--------------|---------|
| p99 spike, kv-hit-rate drop | Kv-hit-rate < 60% | Trigger KV-prefetch + reduce batch size | Targeted prefix prefetch or fallthrough canary |
| SLI burn high but kv healthy | queue depth > 200 | Reduce batch and raise priority for latency-tenants | Emergency scale-up |
| Persistent p99 with CPU/GPU saturation | node_util > 92% | Burst to dedicated capacity | Controlled tenant throttling |

Post-incident tasks and retro:
1) Within 24h: Owner files incident summary including timeline, actions taken, and primary metric graphs.
2) Within 72h: Root cause analysis (RCA) with teams: serving-runtime, eng-platform, observability.
3) Action items: prioritize improvements (examples below).

Suggested long-term improvements (examples):
- Invest in adaptive priming ML model to predict hot prefixes and prefetch proactively (owner: Eng-Platform + Research).
- Reduce cold-start kernel jitter by adding persistent kernel warmers on hot nodes (owner: Serving Runtime).
- Add automated quality-sanity circuits to verify fallthrough variant quality before traffic ramp.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Stage: runbook dry-runs in staging using synthetic workload generator (use job id: priming-dryrun-YYYYMMDD). Verify KV hit-rate increases and p99 drop in 90% of runs.
- Canary: enable automated priming in one low-risk region and measure SLI impact over 2 weeks.
- Global: after 2 successful canaries and one postmortem of a simulated incident, flip automation to Enabled-by-default with operator override.

Appendix A — Example dashboards and queries:
- KV hit-rate: metric name: rw.kv.cache.hit_rate; dim: tenant_id, prefix. Example query: avg_over_time(rw.kv.cache.hit_rate{route="routes/text-gen-interactive", tenant_id=~"cust-.*"}[1m])
- p99 latency: metric: rw.request.latency_ms, query: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(rw_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, route))

Appendix B — Troubleshooting checklist (short):
- Confirm telemetry liveness.
- Confirm model-variant registry reachable and variant image digest matches expected.
- If prefetch aborted, verify GPU memory headroom; restart prefetch with smaller synthetic requests.
